# Review walk

## Pass 0

- **T1-CST-05** — The runner must be able to observe the property asserted. (severity: blocker, flag: auto)
  - ↳ **T2-ACC-01** — Query by role first; test id is the last resort. (severity: major, flag: auto-unless-listed)
  - ↳ **T2-ACC-02** — Every interactive element under test is asserted to have an accessible name. (severity: major, flag: auto-unless-listed)
  - ↳ **T2-ACC-04** — At least one axe (or equivalent) scan runs the full ruleset in a real browser. (severity: major, flag: auto)
  - ↳ **T2-ACC-05** — Do not treat a green axe run as "accessible". (severity: major, flag: auto-unless-listed)
  - ↳ **T2-INTG-01** — Integration means the real dependency engine, at the version production runs. (severity: blocker, flag: auto)
  - ↳ **T2-INTG-02** — Schema and migrations are applied by the same mechanism production uses. (severity: major, flag: argued)
  - ↳ **T2-PERF-02** — Always load/stress test a Release build, never Debug or Development-mode configuration. (severity: major, flag: auto)
  - ↳ **T2-SNAP-06** — Snapshot only stable, non-visual, serialised artifacts; never a component tree. (severity: major, flag: auto)
- **T1-ISO-09** — Before calling a red run a regression, record the failing *fraction* and reproduce on the unmodified baseline. (severity: major, flag: argued)
  - ↳ **T2-PERF-09** — Investigate every sudden performance regression rather than dismissing it as noise, and keep the perf suite from going stale. (severity: major, flag: argued)
- **T1-CST-03** — The default gate's exclusions are derived, not hand-typed, and the count delta proves it. (severity: major, flag: auto)
  - ↳ **T2-ARCH-05** — The forbidden/allowed list is derived from what the repo actually contains, and drift fails the build. (severity: major, flag: auto)
  - ↳ **T2-INTG-07** — The integration lane is excluded from the PR gate only if what it covers is named, and it runs somewhere on a schedule. (severity: major, flag: auto-unless-listed)
  - ↳ **T2-PERF-07** — Tier performance testing by pipeline stage: a fast smoke check gates PR/merge; heavier soak/load tests run nightly or per release, out-of-band. (severity: major, flag: argued)
- **T1-CST-04** — What the gate cannot see is named in writing: coverage per risk area, production types with no test at all, and each gate's blind spot. (severity: major, flag: argued)
  - ↳ **T2-INTG-06** — Record what the emulator does not model. (severity: major, flag: auto-unless-listed)

## Pass 1

- **T1-ORC-01** — Every test asserts something that can distinguish right from wrong. (severity: blocker, flag: auto)
  - ↳ **T2-ETE-09** — E2E sources carry a typed lint that fails on a missing `await`. (severity: major, flag: auto)
  - ↳ **T2-UNIT-05** — Many assertions is fine; many indistinguishable assertions is not. (severity: minor, flag: argued)
- **T1-ORC-06** — Prove the arrange actually reaches the branch under test. (severity: blocker, flag: argued)
  - ↳ **T2-TIME-08** — Derive a poll or watchdog tick from its own timeout, so the check granularity scales with it; pin the derivation with a short-timeout test. (severity: major, flag: argued)
  - ↳ **T2-TIME-09** — Pin a periodic/cyclic timer's cadence with split advances; one large advance cannot observe the tick size. (severity: major, flag: argued)
- **T1-ORC-07** — The asserted observable must have been produced by the act. (severity: blocker, flag: argued)
- **T1-STR-02** — No degenerate fixture: the parameter under test is at a value where the mechanism can be observed at all. (severity: blocker, flag: argued)
  - ↳ **T2-PRP-03** — Bound the generator to the domain; an unbounded generator tests the framework's arithmetic instead of the code. (severity: major, flag: argued)
  - ↳ **T2-UNIT-07** — Tighten a constraint deliberately (pool of 1, capacity of 1) to surface leaks and races in a test rather than in production. (severity: minor, flag: argued)
- **T1-PRF-03** — A filtered or scoped check asserts a non-zero subject count before it can pass. (severity: blocker, flag: auto)
  - ↳ **T2-ARCH-02** — A rule over an empty matched-type set passes: assert the subject count is non-zero first. (severity: blocker, flag: auto)
  - ↳ **T2-ARCH-03** — Where the rule lives determines whether it can fire. (severity: blocker, flag: argued)
- **T1-DBL-01** — A double standing in for a real backend is bound by one contract suite executed against both, and a meta-test fails when a port has no such binding. (severity: blocker, flag: auto)
  - ↳ **T2-CTR-03** — The contract is verified against real provider code, never against a document or a mock of the provider. (severity: blocker, flag: auto)
  - ↳ **T2-CTR-04** — Any in-process double standing in for a remote provider is bound by the same contract suite as the real client. (severity: blocker, flag: auto)
  - ↳ **T2-CTR-06** — A schema/contract test proves the contract rejects the wrong shape, not only that it accepts the right one. (severity: major, flag: auto)

## Pass 2

- **T1-ISO-01** — Never assert on wall-clock time: no millisecond budget, no p95, no ratio of one duration to another. A real budget lives in a dedicated lane, excluded from the default run. (severity: blocker, flag: auto)
- **T1-ISO-02** — Never sleep to synchronise. Poll a condition with a timeout, gate on a latch the test controls, or sync on a signal the system itself emits. (severity: blocker, flag: auto-unless-listed)
- **T1-ISO-03** — Non-determinism enters through an injected, pinned source: an injected clock for time, a seeded generator for randomness — and the instant and the seed are printed on failure. (severity: blocker, flag: auto)
- **T1-ISO-04** — Culture, timezone and locale are pinned wherever the test parses, formats, sorts or compares text, dates or money — and at least one case runs under a non-default one. (severity: major, flag: auto)
- **T1-ISO-05** — Tests pass in any order and alone. No shared mutable state without an unconditional reset. (severity: blocker, flag: auto)
- **T1-ISO-06** — Every shared external resource is namespaced per run or per worker and destroyed on teardown: port, path, database, container, volume, queue, task hub, orchestration instance. (severity: blocker, flag: auto)
- **T1-ISO-07** — No test reads ambient environment: no hardcoded absolute paths, no inherited env vars, no host network, no real credentials, no live third-party. (severity: major, flag: auto)
  - ↳ **T2-ETE-01** — Web-first, retrying assertions only. (severity: blocker, flag: auto)
  - ↳ **T2-ETE-02** — No duration-based wait, and no network-quiet signal, as a readiness check. (severity: major, flag: auto)
  - ↳ **T2-ETE-04** — Each spec is fully isolated: its own context, its own stubs, no ordering dependency. (severity: major, flag: auto-unless-listed)
  - ↳ **T2-INTG-04** — Wait on a readiness signal, never on a delay; wait before the first call, not after the first failure. (severity: blocker, flag: auto-unless-listed)
  - ↳ **T2-INTG-05** — Each test or class gets its own namespace inside the shared dependency: its own database, schema, prefix, or container. (severity: blocker, flag: auto)
  - ↳ **T2-INTG-08** — One shared expensive fixture per class, disposed deterministically; never one container per test method. (severity: minor, flag: argued)
  - ↳ **T2-PERF-03** — Define explicit pass/fail thresholds on the load test itself — not eyeballing a report — and only inside the performance lane (ruling C17). (severity: major, flag: auto)
  - ↳ **T2-PERF-05** — Wire thresholds into the normal test-framework assertions so they gate CI like any other test — inside this lane only (ruling C17). (severity: major, flag: auto)
  - ↳ **T2-PRP-05** — Fix the seed and the case count in CI, and print both. (severity: major, flag: auto)
  - ↳ **T2-SNAP-03** — Scrub every non-deterministic field before comparing: ids, timestamps, ordering, machine names, paths. (severity: blocker, flag: auto)
  - ↳ **T2-TIME-01** — Specifically exercise midnight, month/day boundaries, DST transitions, and leap years with the fake clock. (severity: major, flag: auto-unless-listed)
  - ↳ **T2-TIME-02** — Never mix a real clock and a fake one in the same test. (severity: major, flag: auto)
  - ↳ **T2-TIME-03** — For precise business-logic/timer tests, advance fake time explicitly and deliberately, per test, rather than relying on auto-advance. (severity: major, flag: argued)
  - ↳ **T2-TIME-04** — For UI/debounce-style dependence, prefer a clock that auto-advances realistically and flush on a condition — never a tick to an arbitrary fixed value. (severity: major, flag: argued)
  - ↳ **T2-TIME-05** — Dispose timers created against a fake clock in teardown, the same as any other resource. (severity: major, flag: auto)
  - ↳ **T2-TIME-07** — An advance issued immediately after starting an async host or loop is silently lost; sync on the subject's own emitted signal, never on a fixed delay. (severity: blocker, flag: argued)
  - ↳ **T2-UNIT-06** — Lane speed is a lane-level report, never a per-test assertion. (severity: minor, flag: auto)
- **T1-ISO-08** — "Flaky" is a measured, quarantined, expiring state — never a retry budget. (severity: major, flag: argued)
  - ↳ **T2-ETE-06** — Trace on first retry; retries are bounded and are not a flake-hiding device. (severity: major, flag: auto-unless-listed)

## Pass 3

- **T1-SCO-02** — The test's name is a claim; the body proves every half of it. (severity: blocker, flag: argued)
- **T1-SCO-01** — Name the one-line production edit that reddens this test; if the only edit you can name is an intentional decision, it is a change detector, not a test. (severity: blocker, flag: argued)
  - ↳ **T2-SNAP-01** — A snapshot is a change detector by construction; use it only where the whole shape is the contract. (severity: major, flag: argued)
  - ↳ **T2-SNAP-02** — Pair every snapshot with explicit assertions on the business facts that matter. (severity: major, flag: argued)
- **T1-SCO-03** — Test observable behaviour through the surface a caller uses; no reflection into privates, and no test-only seam on a production type. (severity: major, flag: auto)
  - ↳ **T2-BDD-05** — Write Gherkin declaratively — describe behaviour, not implementation. (severity: major, flag: argued)
  - ↳ **T2-BDD-06** — Push interaction mechanics down into step definitions; keep the scenario text implementation-agnostic. (severity: major, flag: auto-unless-listed)
  - ↳ **T2-ETE-03** — Locate by user-visible role or label, not CSS or XPath. (severity: major, flag: auto-unless-listed)

## Pass 4

- **T1-ORC-02** — The expected value is derived independently of the code under test. (severity: blocker, flag: argued)
  - ↳ **T2-PERF-08** — Derive a baseline from multiple runs, not one, and gate on a percentage deviation from it rather than a single hard number. (severity: major, flag: argued)
  - ↳ **T2-PRP-01** — Reach for a property test when a law exists; otherwise write examples. (severity: minor, flag: argued)
- **T1-ORC-03** — Assert the tightest predicate the contract allows: no slack a plausible regression fits through, and an exact count wherever the count is the contract. (severity: blocker, flag: argued)
  - ↳ **T2-ACC-07** — Assert the association, not the presence, of a label or description. (severity: major, flag: auto-unless-listed)
  - ↳ **T2-PERF-04** — Assert on percentiles and error rates, not averages. (severity: major, flag: argued)
- **T1-ORC-04** — A negative or absence assertion is paired with a positive that proves the code ran. (severity: blocker, flag: auto)
  - ↳ **T2-TIME-06** — Positively assert that time-gated behaviour does not happen before its trigger, not only that it does happen after. (severity: blocker, flag: auto)
- **T1-ORC-05** — Exception assertions name the exact type and the discriminating detail; every narrowed production catch filter gets a negative test. (severity: major, flag: auto)

## Pass 5

- **T1-DBL-02** — A double's behaviour is a claim about production: it honours every parameter the real thing honours, is concurrency-safe when the SUT fans out, and is never degenerate. (severity: blocker, flag: argued)
- **T1-DBL-03** — Stub at a boundary you own, at the lowest level that removes the cost, and never in the pure-domain layer. (severity: major, flag: auto)
  - ↳ **T2-CTR-02** — Consumer-driven by default; bi-directional spec comparison only when the provider is third-party or will not run verification. (severity: minor, flag: argued)
  - ↳ **T2-ETE-05** — Third-party and backend calls are stubbed at the route/transport level. (severity: major, flag: auto)
  - ↳ **T2-UNIT-02** — "Must mock everything" is a coupling finding about the production type, not a testing rule to work around. (severity: major, flag: argued)
- **T1-DBL-04** — A mock earns an assertion only when the call is itself the observable contract; never assert call sequences or counts as a proxy for an outcome. (severity: major, flag: argued)

## Pass 6

- **T1-SCO-04** — A failure-path test asserts the state of the thing that failed, not only the flag raised beside it. (severity: blocker, flag: argued)
  - ↳ **T2-ARCH-06** — Do not reach for an architecture rule to express a data-flow property inside a method body. (severity: major, flag: argued)
- **T1-SCO-05** — Every reachable state has a test: empty, loading, partial, error, success, and the states reached only by failure or by a human not answering. (severity: blocker, flag: argued)
  - ↳ **T2-ACC-03** — Accessibility is a failing test, not a review item, and every reachable state of a view is scanned — not just the happy one. (severity: blocker, flag: auto-unless-listed)
  - ↳ **T2-ACC-06** — The keyboard path is tested separately from the mouse path. (severity: major, flag: argued)
  - ↳ **T2-ETE-08** — Routing, unknown routes, and the error boundary each have an e2e test. (severity: major, flag: auto-unless-listed)
- **T1-SCO-06** — Every rule, filter, allowlist or predicate has at least one test driving the real production input-building path. (severity: blocker, flag: argued)
- **T1-SCO-07** — Assert at least one secondary observable: a neighbouring field, an emitted event, a counter, related state. (severity: major, flag: argued)
- **T1-CST-06** — Wiring and registration have a smoke test: dropping a registration must fail something. (severity: major, flag: auto)
  - ↳ **T2-CTR-05** — Where no contract test exists, a derivation check is the minimum: the client's route/DTO set is generated from, or diffed against, the server's. (severity: major, flag: auto)

## Pass 7

- **T1-CST-01** — Every test declares its size, and the size's constraints are enforced. (severity: major, flag: auto)
- **T1-STR-01** — One act, visibly separated arrange/act/assert, no control flow in the body except idiomatic parametrization, and the varied input readable at the call site. (severity: minor, flag: auto-unless-listed)
- **T1-STR-03** — A skipped test carries a reason, a tracking id and a re-enable condition; its code is unverified until it runs. (severity: major, flag: auto)
  - ↳ **T2-BDD-09** — A dormant (`@ignore`/skipped) scenario's step bindings are unverified code; un-ignoring is a required step of the change that lifts the block, not a follow-up. (severity: major, flag: auto)
  - ↳ **T2-PERF-01** — Load tests validate a response-time goal under specified normal concurrent load; stress tests validate stability and graceful recovery under extreme load. Keep the two goals distinct. (severity: major, flag: argued)
  - ↳ **T2-SNAP-05** — Keep snapshots small enough to read; a growing snapshot count is a quality metric in its own right. (severity: minor, flag: argued)
  - ↳ **T2-UNIT-01** — A unit test touches no network, filesystem, database, real clock, ambient env, or thread it did not create. (severity: major, flag: auto)
  - ↳ **T2-UNIT-03** — Vary intersecting properties, not one axis at a time — bugs live at the combinations. (severity: major, flag: argued)
- **T1-CST-02** — Every test names the defect it catches that no cheaper and no existing test catches. (severity: minor, flag: argued)
  - ↳ **T2-BDD-07** — BDD/Gherkin pays off when scenarios stay tied to explicit business goals, not just feature-level examples. (severity: major, flag: argued)
  - ↳ **T2-CTR-01** — Two components that deploy independently need a contract test; two that always ship together do not. (severity: major, flag: argued)
  - ↳ **T2-ETE-07** — E2E covers journeys, not fields. (severity: minor, flag: argued)
  - ↳ **T2-INTG-03** — Assert the thing only the real backend can prove. (severity: major, flag: argued)
  - ↳ **T2-TIME-10** — A shutdown/stop assertion follows the runner's actual chain of state transitions, not the assumption that the first stop call is terminal. (severity: major, flag: argued)
  - ↳ **T2-UNIT-04** — Phase coverage by dependency layer: leaves unmocked, mid-layer with leaves faked, top layer last. (severity: minor, flag: argued)

## Pass 8

- **T1-PRF-01** — Red-proof every new or changed check against the exact expression it targets, and record the mutation and the observed failure. (severity: blocker, flag: argued)
  - ↳ **T2-ARCH-01** — Plant a real violation and watch the rule go red. An architecture rule you have not seen fail is presumed inert. (severity: blocker, flag: argued)
  - ↳ **T2-BDD-03** — Writing or automating a scenario before the production code exists is what makes it BDD; writing scenarios after the code is done is test automation wearing Gherkin. (severity: major, flag: argued)
  - ↳ **T2-PRP-02** — A property must be shown to fail on a seeded bug, like any other check. (severity: blocker, flag: argued)
  - ↳ **T2-PRP-04** — On failure, capture the shrunk counterexample and commit it as a normal example test. (severity: major, flag: argued)
- **T1-PRF-02** — Every claim about the suite is executed, not reasoned. (severity: blocker, flag: argued)
  - ↳ **T2-SNAP-04** — Never bulk-accept. A snapshot diff is reviewed like a code diff, and the acceptance is part of the PR. (severity: blocker, flag: auto-unless-listed)
- **T1-PRF-04** — A gate whose failure blocks nothing is documentation; say so or wire it in. (severity: major, flag: argued)
  - ↳ **T2-ARCH-04** — Prefer the coarser mechanism when it is airtight; keep the finer one only if it demonstrably fires. (severity: major, flag: argued)
  - ↳ **T2-PERF-06** — Know the tool's default abort behaviour: a threshold breach does not necessarily stop the run unless configured to. (severity: major, flag: argued)
